chile/santiago-centro.name: Plaza de Armas and Cerro San Cristobal
chile/santiago-centro.description: The colonial heart of Santiago and a hilltop park with a funicular and a view of the Andes.
chile/santiago-centro.details: Plaza de Armas has the cathedral and the national history museum, and the Mercado Central nearby is the place for seafood. Cerro San Cristobal rises above Providencia with a funicular, a statue of the Virgin and a view of the city and the Andes on clear days. Smog can hide the mountains in winter.

chile/santiago-barrios.name: Bellavista, Lastarria and the markets
chile/santiago-barrios.description: Bohemian neighbourhoods of murals, cafes and bars, plus La Vega fresh market.
chile/santiago-barrios.details: Lastarria and Bellavista have street art, bookshops, wine bars and the house of Pablo Neruda, La Chascona. La Vega Central is a busy market for fruit and everyday food. Evenings are lively and safe in the main streets.

chile/casablanca-wine.name: Casablanca and Maipo Valley wineries
chile/casablanca-wine.description: Cool-climate vineyards for white wines and Carmenere reds within an hour of Santiago.
chile/casablanca-wine.details: Casablanca Valley is known for sauvignon blanc and chardonnay and sits on the way to the coast, and Maipo is famous for cabernet near the city. A winery day gives tastings with lunch. Book through a tour or driver.

chile/valparaiso.name: Valparaiso funiculars and street art
chile/valparaiso.description: A port city of hillside houses, murals, funicular lifts and ocean views, a UNESCO site.
chile/valparaiso.details: Valparaiso spills down steep hills to the Pacific, with colourful houses, ascensores (funicular lifts) and murals around Cerro Alegre and Cerro Concepcion. Neruda La Sebastiana house is a highlight. Wear good shoes for the steep lanes and watch your belongings.

chile/vina-del-mar.name: Vina del Mar and the coast
chile/vina-del-mar.description: A seaside resort city with a flower clock, gardens and beaches, a short bus ride from Valparaiso.
chile/vina-del-mar.details: Vina del Mar has a beach promenade, the Quinta Vergara gardens and the Wulff Castle. It is a more orderly counterpart to Valparaiso. The Pacific water is cold, and fog is common in the morning.

chile/valle-de-la-luna.name: Valle de la Luna
chile/valle-de-la-luna.description: A desert landscape of salt formations and dunes near San Pedro de Atacama, best at sunset.
chile/valle-de-la-luna.details: The Moon Valley is a protected area of eroded rock, sand dunes and salt crusts. Most visits end with sunset from a viewpoint on the Amphitheatre, with colour shifting across the Andes. Bring water, sun cream and a jacket for after dark.

image.title: File:Valle De La Luna, II Región, Chile (Unsplash).jpg
image.author: Marcelo Hernán Arre Márfull mham

chile/el-tatio.name: El Tatio geysers
chile/el-tatio.description: A high-altitude geyser field best seen at dawn, with steam columns in freezing air.
chile/el-tatio.details: El Tatio sits at about 4,300 metres and the geysers erupt most strongly in the cold dawn. Tours leave around 4am, so dress in very warm layers and expect altitude effects. Some tours include a hot-spring dip and breakfast.

chile/atacama-lagoons-salar.name: Atacama Salt Flat and altiplanic lagoons
chile/atacama-lagoons-salar.description: A salt flat with flamingos and high mountain lakes beneath volcanoes.
chile/atacama-lagoons-salar.details: The Salar de Atacama has flamingos at Laguna Chaxa. Further up, the Altiplanic lagoons at Miscanti and Meniques are bright blue under volcanic peaks at over 4,000 metres. Most tours combine them with stops in small villages.

chile/atacama-stargazing.name: Atacama stargazing
chile/atacama-stargazing.description: One of the clearest night skies on earth, seen through telescopes with an astronomer.
chile/atacama-stargazing.details: The dry air and altitude of the Atacama give extraordinary star visibility. Evening tours from San Pedro use telescopes and explain the southern constellations. The Milky Way is especially good around new moon. Dress warmly, because nights are very cold.

chile/lagunas-cejar.name: Cejar Lagoon and floating
chile/lagunas-cejar.description: A salt lagoon where you float like in the Dead Sea, followed by a sunset at Tebinquiche.
chile/lagunas-cejar.details: Laguna Cejar is so salty that swimmers float effortlessly. The tour usually adds the Ojos del Salar sinkholes and sunset drinks at Laguna Tebinquiche. Rinse off with fresh water afterwards. Check that the lagoons are open to bathing, because access rules change.

chile/torres-base-hike.name: Base of the Towers hike
chile/torres-base-hike.description: The classic day hike in Torres del Paine, to a glacial lake beneath three granite spires.
chile/torres-base-hike.details: The trail from Hotel Las Torres rises through forest and over a moraine to a lake at the foot of the Towers. It is about 18 kilometres return and takes 8 to 9 hours. Weather is changeable and winds strong, so pack layers and waterproofs. Entry to the park requires a ticket.

chile/grey-glacier.name: Grey Glacier and Lake Grey
chile/grey-glacier.description: A boat trip to the face of Grey Glacier, or a walk to the Mirador, with floating icebergs.
chile/grey-glacier.details: Grey Glacier flows into Lake Grey in the west of the park, and icebergs drift across the lake. Boat trips from the Paine Grande area approach the face. A walk to the viewpoint is an easier option. Dress very warm, because wind off the ice is cold.

image.author: NASA Armstrong Flight Research Center / NASA/Jim Ross

chile/paine-viewpoints.name: Torres del Paine viewpoints and wildlife
chile/paine-viewpoints.description: A drive between waterfalls, lakes and viewpoints, with guanacos and condors.
chile/paine-viewpoints.details: A day tour or self-drive visits Salto Grande, Lake Pehoe, Mirador Cuernos and the Lago Sarmiento steppe. Guanaco herds are common and condors circle above. This is a good option for those who prefer a moderate day to a long hike.

chile/milodon-cave.name: Milodon Cave and Puerto Natales
chile/milodon-cave.description: A giant cave where remains of an extinct ground sloth were found, near a quiet port town.
chile/milodon-cave.details: The Cueva del Milodon is a short drive from Puerto Natales and has a replica of the giant sloth. Puerto Natales has a waterfront, restaurants serving lamb and king crab, and outfitters for the park. It is a gentle half-day.
